headline: Independent evidence layers adjudicate contested and unannotated transcript features
label: Multi Evidence Transcript Annotation
summary: Recent preprints and papers test transcript and gene annotations against Ribo-Seq, proteomic, long-read and single-nucleus data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is evaluation of transcript and gene annotation against independent evidence layers. A Drosophila brain study uses improved TEChim software to argue that transposon insertions act as alternative exons in brain transcripts, explicitly rebutting Azad et al. A genome-wide reannotation of the human genome partitions genes into coding, non-coding and bifunctional classes, identifying approximately 4000 bifunctional genes and providing a searchable database. A preprint proposes a coefficient-of-variation filter for RNA-seq that retains low-expressed, consistent genes, integrating bulk and single-nucleus Arabidopsis data. InspectorORF pairs Ribo-Seq reads with RNA-seq, proteomic and long-read data to validate novel open reading frames, the clearest instance of multi-layer validation. The items are heterogeneous in scope, and the coefficient-of-variation filter addresses integration rather than annotation directly. What is new across these items is cross-dataset comparison used to adjudicate contested or unannotated transcript features.
